title: Hosted member Chat lane times out before the owned Chrome CDP endpoint appears
surface: Guarded hosted native member Chat acceptance
auth_mode: designated existing non-admin reviewer; native authentication not reached
organization_context: Approved organization fixture and membership passed the private preflight; the extension did not launch, so no organization was selected and no organization header was observed.
preconditions: Release v0.2.523 Store artifact 12112098474 is verified against source 580738d3c86f14cba3fa4c8157364340d46f78bb.
Guarded lane A source, capacity, exact artifact and reviewer-link checks pass.
The designated reviewer identity passes the existing private non-admin and approved-organization dry run; a fresh one-use link is staged only for this workflow and removed after terminal failure.
reproduction: Dispatch lane A member-chat through scripts/hosted-release-member-admission.mjs for release run 39063179335 and artifact 12112098474.
Observe package and browser preparation finish with valid resource finals; the native step enters owned_profile.
Observe owned Chrome spawn without launch failure, stderr, crash or sandbox indicators, followed by no DevTools endpoint after about 8 seconds.
Observe the runner summary end unverified at owned_profile and the acceptance resource journal finalize invalid after the child exits.
expected: The admitted owned browser exposes its CDP endpoint so native extension authentication and the member Chat acceptance can begin, or the startup failure is precisely classified without claiming product behavior.
actual: Run 39064545122 ended with summary failure_code unclassified_failure and BROWSER_STARTUP_FAILURE owned_cdp_endpoint_timeout at 8019 ms. Chromium was observed spawned; stderr and listed launch/crash/sandbox indicators were absent; 160 endpoint polls elapsed about 8001 ms. No reviewer authentication, Chat UI, selected organization, API request/header, message, assistant reply or terminal event was observed. The guest resource final was admitted=true, resourceInvalid=true, exitCode=3, decision=invalid; package and browser finals were valid.
reproducibility: Observed once in guarded member lane A. The owned-CDP timeout has appeared in prior hosted lanes, but this record does not claim a deterministic member-specific reproduction or establish a causal mechanism.
severity: S2: a native member acceptance attempt cannot reach authentication or product behavior on this run.
priority: P1: diagnose before another member native acceptance attempt.
cause: Unconfirmed. The owned browser process was observed but its DevTools endpoint was not. A later resource sample reported 100% CPU busy with high load after the endpoint timeout; this does not establish that CPU pressure caused the timeout. No endpoint deadline change is supported by this single invalid-resource run.
sibling_census: Owned-CDP startup failures are recorded in other guarded hosted lanes and startup diagnostics. They precede application authentication and product assertions. EXT-D-0230 is a separate guest Chat composer-remount harness defect and was not reached here.
acceptance_criteria: Form and independently review a falsifiable startup hypothesis from this boundary evidence before any retry.
Use a fresh guarded startup diagnostic with retained sanitized endpoint observations and valid resource finals to distinguish endpoint publication from high-CPU host pressure.
Do not increase the endpoint deadline or infer a product failure from the current run.

After the startup boundary is understood and eligible, pass a fresh guarded member Chat run with genuine non-admin auth, explicit selected organization matching request headers, first-message and same-conversation follow-up assistant content, terminal completion, stable server SHA, and valid resource finals.
next_action: The owner will route a targeted owned-CDP startup diagnosis after the urgent EXT-D-0230 guest harness repair; no blind native retry is authorized by this evidence.

transition_history.reason: Guarded lane A failed before authentication because owned Chrome did not expose its DevTools endpoint within the existing deadline; resource final invalid, no product behavior observed.
